recent_posts.title: 7.29.0 Released: The last Babel 7 minor release · Babel
recent_posts.summary: Babel 7.29.0 marks the final minor release of Babel 7 as the team prepares for Babel 8.0.0. This release adds support for defining transpilation targets via a data-target attribute in @babel/standalone and introduces async API support. Babel 8.0.0-rc.1 is now available for testing, featuring ESM-only packages and requiring Node.js 20+. The team has prepared comprehensive migration guides for both users and API consumers to ease the transition from Babel 7 to 8.

recent_posts.title: 7.28.0 Released: `babel.config.ts`, explicit resource management, and discard binding proposal · Babel
recent_posts.summary: Babel 7.28.0 introduces native TypeScript configuration file support with babel.config.ts and babel.config.mts, enables ES2026 explicit resource management by default in preset-env, adds support for the discard binding proposal using void syntax, and introduces a new commonjs source type option for CommonJS-specific environments like Node.js.

recent_posts.title: Announcing Babel 8 Beta · Babel
recent_posts.summary: Babel 8 Beta has been released after nearly two years of development, featuring ESM-only packages and numerous breaking changes designed for easy migration. The team has removed significant technical debt accumulated during Babel 7's lifetime and provides comprehensive migration guides for both users and API developers. Key improvements include better Node.js compatibility with require(esm) support and streamlined architecture, though the release requires community testing before reaching stability.

recent_posts.title: 7.27.0 Released: better ecosystem alignment · Babel
recent_posts.summary: Babel 7.27.0 enhances ecosystem alignment without significant new features. The code printer now defaults to the correct import attributes syntax. The @babel/preset-typescript's rewriteImportExtensions option has been adjusted for TypeScript alignment. The estree compatibility plugin in @babel/parser generates AccessorProperty nodes for class properties from the decorators stage 3 proposal. Plugin authors can find the full changelog on GitHub.

recent_posts.title: 7.26.0 Released: stage 4 features enabled by default, and a new experimental code printer · Babel
recent_posts.summary: Babel 7.26.0 introduces new default features including support for ECMAScript proposals like import attributes and inline regular expression modifiers. It also includes async hooks for plugins and an experimental mode to preserve token positions in transformed output. Significant changes involve the renaming of some plugins and alignment with TypeScript for rewriting .ts extensions in dynamic imports.

recent_posts.title: 7.25.0 Released: Safari bugfixes and duplicated named capturing groups · Babel
recent_posts.summary: Babel 7.25.0 introduces support for duplicated named capturing groups in regular expressions, a fix for class field issues in Safari, and improvements for JSON module imports to CommonJS. The support for duplicated named capturing groups allows re-using the same name for groups within alternative branches of a regex. Additionally, the update includes a new package to handle class field initializer issues in Safari versions up to 16. Configuration files are also now supported in @babel/node's --eval mode. You can refer to the full changelog on GitHub.

recent_posts.title: 7.24.0 Released: Decorator updates and JSON modules imports · Babel
recent_posts.summary: Babel 7.24.0 has been released with updates to decorators, support for importing JSON modules, and the addition of the Hermes-based Flow parser.

recent_posts.title: CVE-2023-45133: Finding an Arbitrary Code Execution Vulnerability In Babel · Babel
recent_posts.summary: A vulnerability in Babel allows for arbitrary code execution, which was assigned the identifier CVE-2023-45133. The proof of concept for the exploit involves using the `evaluate` function in Babel. The vulnerability has been patched by the Babel team.

recent_posts.title: 7.23.0 Released: Decorator Metadata and many new `import` features! · Babel
recent_posts.summary: 7.23.0 includes transform support for Decorator Metadata, Source Phase Import, Deferred Import Evaluation, and Optional Chaining Assignment proposals. We also added a transform option to let you use the extension within TypeScript imports. You can load module sources using the syntax, for languages that have a defined source representation.

recent_posts.title: 7.22.0 Released: Explicit Resource Management support and Import Attributes parsing · Babel
recent_posts.summary: Babel 7.22.0 is out, with parsing/transform support for the Explicit Resource Management proposal. We also updated our implementation of decorators following some changes in the proposal. You can donate to us on our Open Collective and, better yet, work with us on the implementation of new ECMAScript proposals directly.

top_posts.title: 7.15.0 Released: Hack-style pipelines, TypeScript const enums and Rhino target support · Babel
top_posts.summary: Babel has added support for top-level await and ergonomic brand checks for private fields. There is also now support for the Hack-style pipeline operator. Babel 8 beta is not ready for release yet, but we are starting to expose the first experimental changes. You can read the whole changelog on GitHub.

top_posts.title: 7.16.0 Released: ESLint 8 and TypeScript 4.5 · Babel
top_posts.summary: Babel 7.16.0 has been released. It includes support for a new variant of the pipeline operator proposal, as well as TypeScript 4.5 compatibility. @babel/eslint-parser now supports ESLint 8. The release also includes two new file extensions: .mts and .cts.

top_posts.title: 7.20.0 Released: Deno target and TypeScript 4.9 · Babel
top_posts.summary: TypeScript 4.9 introduces a new keyword operator that lets you assert that an expression has a given type withuot. You can now use Deno as one of your compilation targets.
